programme.title: Come Dine with Me

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Life is hard, so Callum and Jordan, two emotionally-unassembled young lads from Northern Ireland, start the Funboys' Fun Club: a playgroup for childish young men to engage in wholesome mucking about. But when a juice party goes awry, Callum's ultra-religious fiancée Morgan kicks them out, and the Funboys must search for a new HQ.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: The gang belatedly get involved in the Great Famine, the one thing they didn't need to get involved in. Callum's new job at the Ballymac Folk Museum sends him down a spiral of method acting as a starving peasant. And he's helped along in this grovelling subservience by his new boss, tyrannical land steward Phillip. The sudden news, to Jordan, that a million people died during the potato famine causes him to finally develop empathy, and it turns out to be a real pain.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: Strange things are afoot in Ballymacnoose: animals in small clothing, paranormal sightings of leprechauns, and most bizarrely of all, Callum gets his first ever match on a dating app. The one prickle on the pickle is that Gwen, Callum's dream girl, is also in an open relationship with the 50-year-old Grainne, a woman who disembowels chickens for a living.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: Life in Ballymacnoose becomes very complicated when Callum accidentally walks in on Gemma and Lorcan trying out a new form of lovemaking. The sight triggers a long-buried childhood trauma in Callum and raises uncomfortable questions about the town's deeply repressed relationship with sex. Can Ballymacnoose open its heart to true love? Meanwhile, Jordan has officially begun dating his much older lover, 50-year-old Grainne.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: As Callum begins slowly unravelling under the strain of Jordan's relentless night terrors about baldness, he stumbles upon a flyer for Ballymacbot Wars - a local robot combat tournament offering a generous cash prize and a potential ticket out of Jordan's bedroom. Meanwhile, Jordan is uncharacteristically uninterested in the whole affair. He's become a bald hermit, terrified to leave the house and expose his creamy scalp to the outside world.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: In central England, three culinary heavyweights return to the `Great British Menu' kitchen. Two Michelin star chef Daniel Clifford creates a dish called `A Trip to the Chippy', where nothing is as it first appears. That is also the theme for Michelin star chef Richard Bainbridge's starter, `banana split', while Will Holland offers up goats cheese mousse, balsamic jelly and gingerbread.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Here, the chefs try to impress with their fish courses. Daniel Clifford puts up a creative dish called `Catch of the Day'. Does Richard Bainbridge's dish titled `Tongue in Cheek' live up to its comedy name? Will judge Marcus Wareing find the comedy value in Will Holland's coconut poached brill, crab, celeriac and tomato essence?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The chefs in central England cook their main courses. Daniel Clifford's main has the same title as Richard Bainbridge's fish course, `Tongue in Cheek', but it is a wildly different plate of food; Richard Bainbridge presents guinea fowl in a beef bladder and calls the dish `Which Came First: the Chicken or the Egg'; Will Holland offers roast longhorn beef rib eye, bread and bone marrow pudding and parsley paste.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The chefs in central England have one last chance to impress Marcus Wareing before the final two are chosen to face the judging panel. Will Daniel Clifford's `Going Out with a Bang' be good enough? Has Richard Bainbridge dropped the comedy ball with his coffee and chocolate dessert called `Time to Reflect'? Or will an unusual dish of parsnip banoffee cake, chocolate tart and parsnip ice cream get Will Holland through?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's decision time for the chefs from the central England region. Only two chefs remain to cook their entire menus for judges Prue Leith, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton. The panel is joined by guest judge, comedian and actor Jim Moir, known to millions as Vic Reeves.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The South West chefs battle it out for a chance to cook at the special banquet. Will veteran judge Tom Kerridge like Chris Eden's modern twist on `Duck a l'Orange', or will he favour Peter Sanchez-Iglesias' dish called `Picnic'? Perhaps Emily Watkins's witty dish called `Eggs and Ham' will prove a winner.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The South West chefs cook their fish courses here. Cornishman Chris Eden takes inspiration from home to create a lobster and oyster dish called `Gone Surfing', Peter Sanchez-Iglesias cooks up a dish inspired by childhood memories titled `Fish and Chips', while Emily Watkins serves up a dish with cured trout called `High Tea'.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The South West chefs cook their main courses and veteran Tom Kerridge is looking for perfection. Will Chris Eden's spin on a fast food classic simply called `B.L.T' gain top points? programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: For the South West chefs, which dessert will progress? Peach melba, apple pie and `Lolly and Sweets' fight it out.

programme.title: Great British Menu

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The Welsh chefs raise the curtain with their starters, but which one is going to produce a showstopper? programme.title: Kenya Wildlife Diaries

programme.title: Secrets of the Enchanted Forests
programme.desc: Travelling to the Arctic for a peek at the brutal challenges of life in the boreal forest, then admiring some stellar animal adaptations. Witnessing a secret reindeer superpower, navigating a rodent labyrinth of snow, and learning about moose.

programme.title: Nomads of the Serengeti
programme.desc: Wildlife expert and safari guide Jean Du Plessis travels to Mahale Mountains National Park in the hopes of spending time with the wild chimpanzees that live in the forests of this remote and protected corner of Tanzania.

programme.title: Rooted
programme.desc: This is the incredible story of a tree that has been around for eight hundred years - that can withstand the harshest conditions - and that is more loved by insects, birds and animals than any other - the enormous Baobab. Rooted on the savannah of Malilangwe Game Reserve in southern Zimbabwe.

programme.title: Great Parks of Africa
programme.desc: Food, water, and shelter are essential to all life from the smallest of beings to the largest.

programme.title: Tales from Zambia
programme.desc: Everyday in the Luangwa Valley a carcass is sighted. Each body holds the story that lead them to their death. In Safari CSI we investigate what killed three carcasses that have been uncovered.

programme.title: Shark Squad
programme.desc: In some of the most-remote regions on the planet, researchers dive deep and brave danger to unlock secret shark behaviours and fight for the protection of these supreme predators before it is too late.

programme.title: Baby Animals
programme.desc: Watch how animals nurture their young as baby animals including red pandas, snow leopards and rhinos eat sleep and play their way to adulthood.

programme.title: Baby Animals
programme.desc: Watch how animals nurture their young as baby animals including koalas, European elk and Asian small-clawed otters eat sleep and play their way to adulthood.

programme.title: Arctic Secrets
programme.desc: On the north-east coast of Baffin Island, in Canada's Arctic, lies Ninginganiq, a blustery wilderness where only the intrepid travel. In fall, it is so dangerous that even seasoned Inuit sailors keep away.

programme.title: Arctic Secrets
programme.desc: The Hudson Bay lowlands are part of North America's largest wetland. Over 300,000 square kilometers of muskeg, a vast bogland as far as the eye can see characterised by water soaked peat, mosses and stunted trees.

programme.title: America's Wild Border: Northern Exposure
programme.desc: Along the world's longest border between Canada and the USA, wildlife lives in two different worlds. The animals there live on the edge of different habitats with conflicting rules of life.

programme.title: After the Wildfires
programme.desc: Documentary mapping the aftermath of the catastrophic bushfires in Australia. How does nature recover and how do the wildlife in the affected area live?

programme.title: High Life in the Dead Mountains
Untamed Valley
programme.desc: Kasikizi lagoon is home to a small community of diverse wildlife. At the height of the wet season, it's full to the brim with water, and a peaceful spot, ideal for two old male hippos who wallow in its watery depths.

programme.title: Untamed Valley
programme.desc: The Big Bend is over two miles long and meanders along the Luangwa River in Zambia. It's a busy spot, home to a pod of hippos who luxuriate in its deep pools, an important crossing point for elephants and place to drink for huge herds of buffalo.

programme.title: Untamed Valley
programme.desc: Bustling with wildlife, a grassland lies at the heart of Zambia's Luangwa Valley known to locals as the Ebony Plain. It's a busy little neighbourhood and home to a family of warthogs, baboons and a solitary female leopard named Olimba.

programme.title: David Attenborough's Galapagos
programme.desc: Sir David Attenborough explores the volcanic islands and biological wonderland of Galapagos in this three-part documentary. Here, he charts the archipelago's explosive rise from the ocean millions of years ago, and takes a look at its unique wildlife.

programme.title: David Attenborough's Galapagos
programme.desc: David Attenborough stumbles upon species found nowhere else in the world that show how life has to quickly adapt to the islands' ever-changing landscapes.

programme.title: David Attenborough's Galapagos
programme.desc: David Attenborough explores the unusual species that inhabit the unique islands of Galapagos, including giant tortoise Lonesome George.

programme.title: The Bachelor King
programme.desc: David Attenborough takes a bird's-eye view in this spectacular documentary, charting the king penguins' attempts to survive, find love and raise a family in the unforgiving Antarctic.

programme.title: Micro Monsters With David Attenborough
programme.desc: It's a bug-eating world out there, and the documentary continues with a look at how the various critters disable the defences of their respective prey.

programme.title: Deadly Australians
programme.desc: Australia is home to the world's most toxic, venomous and dangerous creatures. From the oceans to the forest, swamps and deserts, it's a continent teeming with a hugely disproportionate number of creatures that can envenomate, poison or maim.

programme.title: Africa's Hunters
programme.desc: Kamuti, an old leopard, struggles to find a meal while hoping to avoid a pride of lions.
